In 1944, the US Treasury Secretary had a plan for post-war Germany:

Delete it as an industrial nation. Forever.

Roosevelt and Churchill both initialed it. Then it leaked.

The Morgenthau Plan — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Henry Morgenthau Jr.'s logic: Germany had started two world wars in 30 years. Disarmament hadn't worked after 1918.

So remove the ability to wage war entirely — dismantle the factories, flood the mines, partition the country, and turn it "primarily agricultural and pastoral."
2/ The plan: Germany split into a North and South state, the Ruhr and Saar — the industrial heart of Europe — stripped and internationalized, East Prussia and Silesia handed to Poland and the USSR.

3/ At the Quebec Conference in September 1944, Roosevelt and Churchill initialed a version of it.

Days later it leaked to the press. Goebbels ran it on every front page: proof the Allies meant to destroy Germany, not just defeat it.

4/ The plan died fast. The War and State Departments revolted; economists pointed out that a de-industrialized Germany meant a starving Europe.

By 1947 the policy had fully reversed: the Marshall Plan would rebuild German industry instead of erasing it.

5/ The map above shows the Germany that almost was.

Instead, the opposite happened: within 15 years West Germany was Europe's industrial engine again — this time inside NATO.

Sometimes the most important maps are the ones that never came true.
